newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL BID TO STAY TOP AT FLORO'S SPORTING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL BID TO STAY TOP AT FLORO'S SPORTING.

text.p: New Spanish league leaders Real Madrid come up against a familiar face in Saturday's game at Sporting Gijon -- their former coach Benito Floro.
The game comes a week after Real displaced Barcelona at the top of the table after hitting their best form yet against Valencia, where another former Real man Jorge Valdano has just taken charge.
Davor Suker shone in the 4-2 victory with a hat-trick that left him within one strike of Spain's top scorer, Barcelona's Ronaldo.

Suker, who is partnered up front by two other competitors for the title of league top scorer -- Montenegrin star Predrag Mijatovic and teenager Raul Gonzalez -- has kept Real's championship hopes alive by finding the target even when his side are not playing well.
And the Croatian international kept his run going with two goals in Wednesday's comfortable 2-0 cup victory over second division Salamanca.
Victory at Sporting will ensure Real stay top until at least December 7 when the host Barcelona, who look likely to score a hatful against bottom-placed Extremadura on Monday.
Sporting also made it through to the second round of the Spanish Cup, but for them it was a very different story.
Their tedious 1-0 home win against Toledo provoked the wrath of Sporting's fans, and the game ended with protests directed at the coach's bench and the president's box.
It's hardly a new situation for Floro.
He endured constant complaints from Real supporters upon joining the club as a surprise signing from Albacete.
Floro talked with a detached, almost academic air that failed to endear him to the fans. He once gave an entire press conference on the importance of the throw-in.
But Floro is best remembered for the disastrous final game of the 1993 season, when defeat at Tenerife handed arch-rivals Barcelona the title for the second consecutive year.
Floro moved back to Albacete, only to find the fans mutinying against their former hero within a matter of weeks.

After finishing 18th last season, Floro had his work cut out at Sporting. But he has failed to stop the rot, and with Sporting in 16th place in a season which sees four teams automatically relegated, there are many who think his days in Gijon are numbered.
